question.worked_solution:
We must bring all variables to one side of the equation and all constants to the other side. 

Notice that we have $17y$ on the left-hand side and $9y$ on the right-hand side. Since the variable on the left-hand side has a larger coefficient, let's bring all the variables to this side.

The first step is to remove the $9y$ from the right-hand side. We do this by subtracting $9y$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}17y & =9y-16 \\ 17y-9y & =9y-16-9y \\ 8y & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $8:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8y & =-16 \\ \frac{8y}{8} & =\frac{(-16)}{8} \\ \frac{\cancel{8}y}{\cancel{8}} & =-2 \\ y & =-2\end{aligned}
$$
